title: Rational power series and its rational function
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], $T$ an indeterminate, $K[T]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $K[[T]]$ the ring of formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series] and $K(T)$ the field of rational functions [def-weil-rational-function-field]. A formal power series $f\in K[[T]]$ is *rational* (over $K$) if there are polynomials $P,Q\in K[T]$ with $Q(0)
eq0$ such that $Qf=P$ in $K[[T]]$. Since $Q(0)
eq0$, $Q$ is a unit of $K[[T]]$ and $f=PQ^{-1}$: $f$ is the Taylor expansion at $T=0$ of the fraction $P/Q$. The *rational function of $f$* is $R_f=P/Q\in K(T)$; it does not depend on the choice of $(P,Q)$, because if also $Q'f=P'$ with $Q'(0)
eq0$, then $PQ'=QfQ'=P'Q$ in $K[[T]]$, hence in $K[T]$, so $P/Q=P'/Q'$ in $K(T)$. The set of rational power series is written $K[[T]]\cap K(T)$. The map $f\mapsto R_f$ is an injective ring homomorphism from $K[[T]]\cap K(T)$ onto the subring of $K(T)$ of rational functions regular at $T=0$, with inverse $N/D\mapsto ND^{-1}$ (the expansion at $T=0$; $D(0)
eq0$ for the reduced denominator $D$): if $Qf=P$ and $Q'g=P'$ then $QQ'(f+g)=PQ'+P'Q$ and $QQ'(fg)=PP'$, and $R_f=R_g$ gives $PQ'=P'Q$, hence $f=PQ^{-1}=P'Q'^{-1}=g$. Through this map a rational power series and its rational function are identified: an assertion about $f$ 'in $K(T)$' (an identity, a value, a substitution, a pole) is the assertion about $R_f$, and an identity in $K(T)$ between rational functions regular at $T=0$ is the same as the identity of their expansions in $K[[T]]$. For a subring $A\subset K$, '$f\in1+TA[[T]]\cap K(T)$' means that $f$ is rational, has all its coefficients in $A$, and has constant coefficient $1$.

source.place: node thm-weil-final, order 2939, clause (i): '$Z(X_0,T)$ ... belongs to $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$', and clauses (ii), (iv), (v), which treat the power series $Z(X_0,T)$ as an element of $\mathbf Q(T)$ (factorization, poles, substitution $T\mapsto q^{-d}T^{-1}$); the convention is spelled out in sk-def-roots/def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction.md ('$Z(T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$ ... any rational series with integer coefficients and constant coefficient one, in the formal power series convention ... $Z(T)=A(T)/B(T)$ as a Taylor series at $T=0$'). Textbook: literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf, §27, Corollary 27.8 and Lemma 27.9, p. 156 ('The power series $Z(X_0,t)$ is a rational function with coefficients in $\mathbf Q$, i.e., it lies in $\mathbf Q(t)$'; 'let $f(t)\in k[[t]]$; if $f(t)\in K(t)$, then $f(t)\in k(t)$').

mathlib_searches.verdict: generalization that specializes in one line: `K⟦X⟧` and `RatFunc K` both embed in the Laurent series `K⸨X⸩` by injective ring homomorphisms, and $K[[T]]\cap K(T)$ is the intersection of their images; see mathlib_match

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: for `f : K⟦X⟧`, '`f` is rational' is `∃ P Q : K[X], Q.coeff 0 ≠ 0 ∧ (Q : K⟦X⟧) * f = (P : K⟦X⟧)` (coercion `Polynomial.coeToPowerSeries.ringHom`, Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Basic.lean:836; `Q` is a unit by `PowerSeries.isUnit_iff_constantCoeff`, Inverse.lean:111), and its rational function is `RatFunc.mk P Q` (= `algebraMap P / algebraMap Q`, `RatFunc.mk_eq_div`, Mathlib/FieldTheory/RatFunc/Basic.lean:543); equivalently `HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries ℤ K f ∈ Set.range (algebraMap (RatFunc K) (LaurentSeries K))`, the two embeddings into `K⸨X⸩` being `HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries` (injective, PowerSeries.lean:90, 97) and the coercion `RatFunc F → F⸨X⸩` (`instance coeToLaurentSeries`, Mathlib/RingTheory/LaurentSeries.lean:372; injective as a ring homomorphism out of a field), which agree on polynomials (`coe_coe`, LaurentSeries.lean:375). Mathlib has no named predicate for this notion
